messages.author: 40f7d34e9dd27d88
messages.subject: linetype 9 and pdf
parts:
hi,

I have a problem similar to this thread:
http://groups.google.com/group/ggplot2/browse_thread/thread/f05bfdcb47612038/d67d3e78c3fc435e

but not on mac (I am using linux) and not with linetype 5, but 9.

Displaying the data works fine, but in the pdf, it's really difficult to
see the line.

ggplot(data.frame(x=1:10, y=1:10)) + geom_line(aes(x,y), linetype=9)
pdf("/tmp/test.pdf")
ggplot(data.frame(x=1:10, y=1:10)) + geom_line(aes(x,y), linetype=9)
dev.off()

especially when using non-black colors:

df <- data.frame(x=rep(1:40, 10), y=rnorm(40, 15, 10), name=as.factor(1:10))
ggplot(df)+geom_line(aes(x,y,color=name, linetype=name))

pdf("/tmp/test.pdf")
ggplot(df)+geom_line(aes(x,y,color=name, linetype=name))
dev.off()


is there any way to solve this besides specifying the linetypes manually?

best regards,
stefan

I though its a ggplot related issue.

Printing normal plot and ggplot with the same data, it is difficult to see
the line in the ggplot graph, but not in the normal plot.

df=data.frame(x=1:20, y=rnorm(20, 10, 15))
pdf("/tmp/test.pdf")
ggplot(df) + geom_line(aes(x,y), linetype=9)
plot(df$x, df$y, type="l", lty=9)
dev.off()

But when I print the pdf file, there is not difference between the two
lines, so maybe it's a problem of my laptop display.

best regards,
stefan

hey,

maybe it is easier to see the differences, when you set the ggplot
background to white too.

library(ggplot2)
theme_set(theme_bw())

or maybe the problem is somewhere on my side. I will try to test in on
windows within the next days.

Attached is a pdf file, with all axes and grids removed and I see a big
difference between the ggplot line on the left side and the normal plot
in the right side.

Maybe I got it:
It depends on the pdf reader. with evince I don't see anything in the
ggplot plot, with okular and acroread the ggplot line is very faint but
with gv it's ok and both lines are equal.

regards,
stefan
